channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Tajikistan Approves Civil Aviation Security Program Until 2030
item.description: The government of Tajikistan has approved the National Civil Aviation Security Program for 2026-2030. The program aims to enhance passenger and aircraft safety, protect citizens' lives and health, and fulfill international obligations. It includes expanding air travel, modernizing infrastructure, and countering modern threats like cyber threats.

item.title: Kazakhstan Appoints New Ambassadors to Morocco and Cuba
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has appointed Ainur Danenova and Olzhas Issabekov as Kazakhstan's new ambassadors to Morocco and Cuba, respectively. The Akorda announced the personnel changes. Danenova will serve as Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary to the Kingdom of Morocco, while Issabekov takes on the same role in the Republic of Cuba.

item.title: Kazakhstan President Reappoints Elvira Azimova as Constitutional Court Chair
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has reappointed Elvira Azimova as the Chairperson of the Constitutional Court. Azimova previously served as the Human Rights Commissioner before heading the Constitutional Court in 2023. Her reappointment signifies continuity in the leadership of the nation's highest court.

item.title: Kazakhstan Appoints New Ambassadors to Morocco and Cuba
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev of Kazakhstan has appointed new ambassadors to the Kingdom of Morocco and the Republic of Cuba. Ainur Danenova will serve as Ambassador to Morocco, while Olzhas Isabekov takes on the role in Cuba. Andrian Yelemesov has been relieved of his duties as Ambassador to Cuba.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Energy Ministry Unveils "Energy AI Kazakhstan" Concept for Digital Transformation
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Energy has presented the "Energy AI Kazakhstan" concept, aiming to create a unified digital environment for artificial intelligence integration in the sector. The concept includes early risk detection for fuel shortages, automated reporting, and industrial safety monitoring, enhancing data analysis and decision-making.

item.title: Tashkent Metro to Introduce 5-Car Trains During Peak Hours
item.description: Tashkent's metro will operate 5-car trains during peak hours following a city council decision. This aims to address overcrowding, with 85.4% of residents reporting issues during morning and evening commutes. The measure will be implemented by November 20, 2026, on key lines, reducing train intervals to 2-3 minutes.

item.title: Binance Aims to Resume Fund Withdrawals Within 24 Hours After Security Breach
item.description: The world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, Binance, plans to gradually resume its withdrawal services within the next 36 hours, pending successful security checks. The company stated it has frozen over half of the stolen funds, with $3 billion recovered, but a significant portion remains with hackers. The US Secret Service is involved in tracking the assets.

item.title: Kazakhstan Caspian Border Guards Detain 126 Poachers, Seize Illegal Fishing Gear
item.description: Caspian Sea border guards in Kazakhstan have detained 126 individuals and seized 44 small vessels during special operations. Authorities confiscated 11.5 kg of narcotics and 88 km of illegal fishing nets. Over 2,300 sturgeon and other fish caught in nets were released back into the wild. Fines totaling over 4.5 million tenge were imposed.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Courts Received Over 199,000 Cases in Nine Months
item.description: Courts in Kyrgyzstan received 199,219 cases and materials between January and September. Including carry-over cases, a total of 216,630 were under review. The Supreme Court chairman urged judges to avoid unjustified delays and adhere to legal timelines to strengthen public trust.

item.title: Afghan UN Envoy Urges End to Taliban Repression and Discrimination
item.description: Afghanistan's UN Representative Nasir Ahmad Faiq called for an end to the Taliban's systematic repression and discrimination, demanding the restoration of fundamental rights, especially for women and girls. He urged support for UN Special Rapporteur Richard Bennett and an independent investigation into rights violations.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Establish Commission to Oversee Public Construction Project Budget
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev announced the creation of a state commission to strictly monitor the spending of the 'Public Construction' program budget. The commission will include heads of sectoral departments, parliament deputies, and public figures. The president declared the upcoming year a year of nationwide construction.

item.title: Poland's Constitutional Tribunal Building Surrounded by Police Amid Judicial Dispute
item.description: Police surrounded Poland's Constitutional Tribunal building in Warsaw after a judge suspended its president and vice-president. The judge cited obstruction of justice. The tribunal's website claims the court was "hijacked," while police stated they were responding to a potential threat. Protesters gathered, and three arrests were made.

item.title: How Free Are Kazakhstan's Citizens?
item.description: This news item poses a question about the level of freedom experienced by citizens in Kazakhstan. It suggests an upcoming discussion or analysis regarding civil liberties and rights within the country.

item.title: CSTO Anti-Drug Operation Uncovers Over 80,000 Suspicious Financial Transactions
item.description: An anti-drug operation by the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) has identified more than 80,000 suspicious financial operations totaling over 1 billion rubles. The preliminary results were announced on October 30, 2026, following the 'Channel-Caspian Beacon' operation. Law enforcement, border, customs, and financial intelligence agencies from CSTO member states participated.

item.title: Kazakh President Orders State Commission to Oversee 'People's Construction' Program Funds
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has ordered the creation of a state commission to monitor the spending of budget funds for the 'Narodnaya Stroyka' ('People's Construction') program. Announced in his October 28 address, the program aims to develop regions and improve citizens' well-being. The commission will include government officials, lawmakers, and public figures.

item.title: Tokayev Plans State Commission to Oversee 'People's Construction' Spending
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev deems it necessary to establish a state commission for controlling budget expenditures within the 'People's Construction' program. The commission will comprise heads of ministries, parliament members, and public figures. The program, announced in his address, focuses on infrastructure development and modernization.

item.title: Kazakhstan to establish special commission to oversee 'People's Construction' funds
item.description: President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev announced the creation of a special commission to control the spending of funds for the new 'Halyktyk Kurylis' program. The commission will include heads of relevant departments, lawmakers, public figures, activists, volunteers, and journalists. The program aims for significant construction in the coming years, with 6.5 trillion tenge allocated from the National Fund by the end of 2029.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan seeks to expand telemedicine cooperation with Turkic nations
item.description: Kyrgyzstan aims to broaden collaboration with Turkic countries in telemedicine, digital health, medical research, and the adoption of modern diagnostic and treatment technologies. Health Minister Damir Osmonov expressed interest in exchanging scientific knowledge and expertise at the Turkic Medical World Congress in Istanbul. The focus is on joint educational programs, professional internships, and academic exchanges to improve healthcare quality.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Establish Special Commission for Budget Spending Oversight
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev announced the need for a special commission to monitor the spending of budget funds allocated for the "People's Construction" program. The commission will include deputies, public figures, activists, volunteers, and journalists.

item.title: UN Reports 400% Increase in Afghanistan's Opium Production Despite Taliban Ban
item.description: Opium production in Afghanistan has surged by 400% in the past year, despite the Taliban's 2022 ban on poppy cultivation. The UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) study indicates a 330% increase in poppy cultivation area. Farmers are reportedly finding ways to circumvent the ban, growing poppies in smaller, hidden plots.

item.title: Xi Jinping Emphasizes Strengthening Intra-Party Governance for Socialism with Chinese Characteristics
item.description: Xi Jinping stressed the importance of continuously advancing comprehensive intra-Party governance to ensure the Communist Party of China (CPC) remains a strong leadership core for socialism with Chinese characteristics. This statement was made at a meeting gathering non-Party figures to discuss a recent CPC Central Committee decision on strengthening Party governance.

item.title: Two Individuals Arrested in Andijan for Attempting to Sell Hashish for $27,000
item.description: Two individuals were apprehended in Andijan while attempting to sell approximately 2 kilograms of hashish for $27,000. The arrests occurred in a restaurant during a transaction with a special buyer. Law enforcement seized the illicit drugs as evidence.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan Aim to Boost Bilateral Trade to $3 Billion
item.description: Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan plan to increase their mutual trade turnover to $3 billion. This goal was announced following a trade and economic mission to Bishkek, where Kazakh companies secured contracts worth $95 million. The mission involved around 80 Kazakh companies across various sectors, fostering new partnerships and increasing goods supply.

item.title: US Plans to Deport Some Afghan Asylum Seekers to Afghanistan
item.description: The US government intends to deport a number of Afghan asylum seekers to Afghanistan, including those who fled after the Taliban takeover. Some sources suggest over 150 Afghans may face deportation, potentially through Pakistan. Advocates urge Congress to grant Temporary Protected Status to shield them from removal.

item.title: Young Man Murdered Near Taliban Checkpoint in Baghlan
item.description: A young man was murdered in Pul-e-Khumri, Baghlan, approximately 17 days ago by unidentified individuals. The killing occurred near a Taliban checkpoint and intelligence office, despite the group's claims of ensuring security. Perpetrators remain at large, highlighting rising insecurity under Taliban rule.

item.title: Tajikistan Plans to Cooperate with Yandex on Artificial Intelligence
item.description: Tajikistan intends to develop cooperation with the Russian company Yandex in the field of artificial intelligence (AI). Negotiations are in the initial stages. The country is also developing interaction with the Eurasian Development Bank and Gazprombank, and is in talks with a Chinese company regarding AI.

item.title: Kazakh Soldier's Medallion Found in Russia Returned to Kazakhstan
item.description: The soldier's medallion of Red Army soldier Abduvali Zhylysbaev, missing for over 70 years, has been handed over to the Kazakh Ambassador in Russia. Zhylysbaev died in 1941. His remains were found in 2014, and after years of searching by relatives and search teams, his medallion will be returned to his family.

item.title: Pakistan Army Spokesperson: Disruptors Benefiting from War Hinder Iran-US Agreement
item.description: A spokesperson for the Pakistan Army stated that disruptive elements, who profit from continued conflict, are obstructing a potential agreement between Iran and the United States. These actors are actively working against diplomatic progress.

item.title: Almaty Court Orders Reconsideration of Afghan Citizen's Asylum Request
item.description: An Almaty court has ordered the employment and social programs department to reconsider an Afghan citizen's request for refugee status. The authorities had previously denied the application. Human rights advocates reported that new circumstances threatening the woman's life upon return to Afghanistan necessitated the appeal.

item.title: First Modern Hematology Center in Kazakhstan Opens in Ust-Kamenogorsk
item.description: The first modern hematology center in Kazakhstan has opened in Ust-Kamenogorsk, equipped with advanced medical technology. Built on funds returned to the state, the center will provide specialized care for complex blood diseases to residents of East Kazakhstan, Pavlodar, and Abai regions. It includes adult and pediatric hematology, cardiology, and bone marrow transplant units.

item.title: European Commission Approves €45 Billion Funding Package for Ukraine Until 2027
item.description: The European Commission has initiated the approval process for a second tranche of €45 billion in loans for Ukraine, intended for disbursement by the end of 2027. A significant portion will support Ukraine's defense industry. This funding is part of a larger €90 billion credit program agreed upon by EU leaders.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Increase Freight Transport Prices to Afghanistan Effective November 7
item.description: Uzbekistan will increase freight transport prices to Afghanistan starting November 7. However, four types of goods will be exempt from these new charges. The updated regulations aim to adjust transit costs for goods moving into Afghanistan.

item.title: Kazakhstan's State Revenue Committee to Launch AI-Powered Fiscal Data Factory
item.description: Kazakhstan's Committee of State Revenues is launching an artificial intelligence-based fiscal data factory to reduce excessive audits for entrepreneurs. This initiative aims to enhance analytics, improve risk detection accuracy, automate processes, and lower business administrative costs. The committee also emphasized the need for clearer taxpayer information.

item.title: New Modern Clinic Opens in Almaty Region's Raimbek District
item.description: A new modern clinic capable of serving 250 patients per shift has opened in the village of Narynkol, the administrative center of the Raimbek district in the Almaty region. The facility, costing 4.1 billion tenge, is equipped with advanced medical equipment and will improve healthcare quality in the mountainous region.

item.title: 90th Anniversary Celebrated for Zylikha Tamshybay, Hero of Socialist Labor
item.description: The 90th birthday of Zylikha Tamshybay, a Hero of Socialist Labor renowned for transforming the 'Enbekshi' state farm, was celebrated in her home village. The event included laying wreaths at her bust, an exhibition of her life and work, and a scientific conference attended by the regional governor.

item.title: Taliban Arrest Three More Residents in Panjshir Amid Intensified Crackdown
item.description: The Taliban have arrested three more residents from Panjshir's Abdullah Khil Valley in connection with a vehicle explosion targeting their fighters. This follows an earlier wave of detentions, bringing the total arrested to at least 27. Sources report increased harassment of locals by newly deployed Taliban units.

item.title: Former Hotel Owned by Nazarbayev's Nephew Sold in Almaty on Third Attempt
item.description: A former hotel, previously owned by the nephew of Kazakhstan's ex-president Nursultan Nazarbayev, has been sold in Almaty. The sale was successfully concluded on the third attempt, indicating previous difficulties in finding a buyer for the property.

item.title: Pentagon Urges European Allies to Soften Rhetoric Towards Russia
item.description: Pentagon officials have asked NATO allies to reduce sharp statements about the threat from Russia, according to Reuters. The US Department of Defense believes such rhetoric can provoke tension and harm European security. Some allies, like Estonia, have rejected the call for restraint.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Amends Rules for Energy Certification of Buildings
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has introduced changes to the procedure for energy certification of buildings, as per a resolution signed by the Cabinet of Ministers chairman. The amendments update regulations on energy efficiency assessment, introducing scales from A to G for various energy consumption indicators, including heating and hot water usage.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Sees Nearly 20% Drop in Inmate Population Due to Probation
item.description: The introduction of a probation mechanism in Kyrgyzstan has led to a nearly 20% reduction in the number of inmates. The Ministry of Justice reported that the recidivism rate among individuals on probation is approximately 1%. The EU-funded 'Justice for All' project is supporting these reforms, including the development of a digital criminal justice ecosystem.
